## How to read these rankings

The field includes 67 Power Four football members, independent Notre Dame, and all 69 Group of Six teams. The November edition scores each job under the October framework. The October rank remains available for all 79 returning programs.

### Source observations, calculations, and judgment

| Layer | Examples | How to interpret it |
|---|---|---|
| Source observations | EADA and NCAA financial records, reported attendance, recruiting ratings, SP+/FPI, disclosed contracts | Values attributed to their original source, year, and definition. Recruiting and performance ratings are themselves evaluations produced by their providers. |
| Calculated comparisons | Multi-year averages, inflation-adjusted spending, national or conference comparisons | Summaries derived from source observations. Their meaning depends on the years covered, formula, and source completeness. |
| Reported estimates | Private-school compensation, NIL/roster spending, undisclosed buyouts | Source-specific estimates with varying confidence, rather than audited or contract-verified amounts. Competing estimates and missing disclosure remain relevant. |
| Editorial judgments | Overall ranks, program tiers, competitive ceiling, and departure probabilities | Our interpretation of the evidence. These require assumptions and may change when new information arrives. |

### Ranking framework

Each category receives a score on a 0–100 scale. The weighted sum determines rank. Nine tiers use one scoring scale across all 137 jobs. Tiers 1 through 8 start at 90, 82, 75, 68, 61, 52, 40, and 29 points, respectively. Tier 9 covers scores below 29. All 67 Power Four jobs fall into the first six bands.

| Category | Editorial emphasis | Considerations |
|---|---:|---|
| Football resources | 30% | Football budget, staff pay, roster spending, facilities, donor support |
| Recruiting geography | 20% | Access to high school and transfer talent |
| Conference and realignment | 20% | Media revenue, CFP access, future league stability |
| Fans and tradition | 15% | Engagement, history, institutional priorities |
| Competitive ceiling | 15% | Sustainable success potential, difficulty of league |

### How we scored the November field

Football resources gives 50% of its weight to FY2022–24 football spending, 18% to head and assistant coach pay and football coaching payroll, 12% to available football roster estimates and direct revenue sharing, 12% to FY2025 athletics spending, and 8% to donations. Each finance source is ranked separately before combining scores. Roster estimates use available point estimates or midpoints of reported ranges.

Recruiting gives 38% to the average number of geocoded top-1,000 prospects per class within 250 miles in 2021–25, 32% to recruiting class rank in those years, 20% to 2026 roster talent and 10% to incoming transfer quality. Nearby prospects can count for competing schools. This favors access to talent and gives national recruiters credit through their actual classes.

Conference platform scores are editorial assumptions about media resources, exposure and stability. The SEC and Big Ten score 100, independent Notre Dame 95, the ACC and Big 12 78, the American and Pac-12 44, the Mountain West and Sun Belt 33, and the MAC and C-USA 26. The dashboard also ranks every job with this component removed, holding the other four scores fixed.

Fan support and tradition combines recent home crowds (37%), 2010–19 crowds (16%), stadium capacity (12%), FY2025 ticket revenue (10%) and all-time winning percentage (25%). Winning history includes earlier subdivisions. Competitive ceiling gives 72% to national strength and 28% to standing among current conference peers. National strength blends 2016–25 SP+ and FPI with the November 21 Sagarin rating. Ten historical FBS seasons earn the full 75% historical weight, with older ratings receiving proportionally less weight for shorter histories. Notre Dame uses national standing in both parts.

Metrics are converted to percentiles among observed schools, averaging ties. For sparsely disclosed pay, roster, donations, ticket sales and talent metrics, those percentiles are mapped onto the reporting schools’ range of football spending, crowds or recruiting rank as applicable. Within each category, remaining inputs share the weight of unavailable measures. A reported school-wide budget and football-only spending each retain their own comparison. Facilities quality, donor willingness, service-academy requirements and contract terms remain considerations a particular coach may value differently.

The November score puts South Florida and Boise State just below Kansas, the lowest-ranked Power Four job. Removing the conference weight puts both ahead of Kansas. That distinction matters more than the fraction of a point separating the two G6 leaders.

### Evidence and limitations

Use the five framework categories to compare key metrics across programs. Select a school to expand the evidence behind each category. The downloads include the source registry, reporting definitions, coverage, and unresolved conflicts. [Download the full scoring inputs](../assets/coaching/program_inputs.csv).

School details show the expanded FY2025 NCAA and EADA reports side by side in nominal dollars. Each source retains its own accounting definitions. Across the two panels, every G6 program has a FY2025 football spending observation. EADA has no usable report for the three service academies, whose spending appears in the NCAA panel. Verified FY2025 athletics ticket sales and contributions feed the November model. FY2025 football coaching compensation appears in the school details. The coaching payroll input to the model uses the FY2022–24 average.

Peer comparisons use the observed sample for each metric across the full rankings, the Power Four, the Group of Six and the school's current conference. Missing figures are excluded from those sample sizes. NCAA athletics-wide coaches compensation, football-only payroll and assistant salary pools cover different scopes. Attendance includes official totals and reconstructed observations. NIL estimates can refer to different measures of spending.

All 137 programs have regional recruiting, high-school class, 2026 roster talent, incoming transfer counts, November Sagarin and 2025 home attendance observations. Incoming transfer quality is available for 134. North Dakota State and Sacramento State have November Sagarin ratings and joined the FBS in 2026, after the 2016–25 SP+ and FPI window. Other recently promoted schools can have shorter FBS histories.

The carousel probabilities are separate editorial forecasts for the stated deadline, informed by attributed reporting, results, contracts and buyout costs, and institutional circumstances. Fan sentiment and unsourced speculation carry less weight than original reporting or official statements. A coach’s intention to return does not establish an institutional guarantee. Announced departures are distinguished from forecasts.
